description: Official repo for paper "Structured 3D Latents for Scalable and Versatile 3D Generation" (CVPR'25 Spotlight).

summary.one_liner: TRELLIS is Microsoft's official research code and pretrained models for generating 3D assets from text or image prompts, output as radiance fields, 3D Gaussians, or meshes.
summary.what_it_does: The repo provides the TRELLIS large 3D generation model, built on a unified Structured LATent (SLAT) representation that can be decoded into multiple output formats. It offers image-to-3D and text-to-3D pipelines, with pretrained models up to 2B parameters trained on the TRELLIS-500K dataset. Outputs can be rendered to videos, exported as GLB meshes, or saved as PLY Gaussians. The README also mentions multi-image conditioning for the image model, variant generation, and local 3D editing. It includes a Gradio web demo (app.py) and training code driven by train.py with JSON configs.
use_cases: generate 3D models from a single image
export textured GLB meshes for games or graphics pipelines
produce 3D Gaussian splats or radiance fields
generate variants of an existing 3D asset
fine-tune or train large 3D generative models
notable: Unified Structured LATent (SLAT) representation decodes to Radiance Fields, 3D Gaussians, and meshes from one latent
Pretrained models from 342M to 2.0B parameters, hosted on Hugging Face
Released TRELLIS-500K dataset curated from Objaverse(XL), ABO, 3D-FUTURE, HSSD, and Toys4k
Supports local 3D editing and variant generation, per the README
Training configs and code provided for VAEs and flow transformers
caveats: Tested only on Linux; Windows setup is not fully tested according to the README
Requires an NVIDIA GPU with at least 16GB memory and a CUDA Toolkit for compiling submodules
The README recommends image-conditioned models over text-conditioned ones, which it describes as less creative and detailed
